TypeScript

Make data contracts clearer across a growing codebase.

TOfficial product ↗Open in the hierarchy →
Level 4Inspect the detail

TypeScript adds a type system to JavaScript development. We can define the expected shape of customer records, application responses, and component inputs so engineers catch many mismatches during development. It is particularly useful when a product connects several APIs or grows across teams, because the code expresses assumptions that otherwise live only in informal documentation.

Useful outputs

  • Typed business models and interfaces
  • Type-check configuration and CI command
  • Clear contracts between application modules

Where we can apply it

  • CRM integration: response schema → typed model → validated UI fields.
  • Product change: contract update → compiler feedback → reviewed adaptation.
  • Team handover: shared types → documented assumptions → safer maintenance.
01

Use case 1

Define shared models for leads, accounts, subscriptions, and workflow states.

02

Use case 2

Catch incompatible interface props and API assumptions before release.

03

Use case 3

Improve refactoring confidence when features change across multiple modules.

Inputs we need

  • Existing JavaScript code or application specification
  • API response schemas and business entities
  • Build pipeline and code review conventions

Delivery sequence

  • Identify important data boundaries and model expected values.
  • Apply types and handle optional fields and error cases explicitly.
  • Run type checks in delivery and review external data validation separately.

Expert review points

  • Review overly broad types that hide useful errors.
  • Validate untrusted inputs at runtime as well as in development.
